To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
health risk assessments can be used to promote healthy behaviours, improve health and reduce healthcare costs.
health risk assessments with a focus on family health history are feasible, and can have a significant impact on patient knowledge, behaviour and clinical outcomes.

(1) family health history collection in the context of health risk assessment is feasible and can be performed in the clinical setting, (2) family health history information is useful in identifying patients at risk for common conditions, (3) family health history is useful in identifying risk for rare disease, (4) patients are receptive to health risk assessments and family health history collection, (5) patients are receptive and responsive to genetic risk information and (6) patients are receptive but not responsive to lifestyle risk
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of health risk assessments that are easy and enjoyable for patients to complete, that can be integrated into clinical workflow and that can be used by patients and providers to identify and address risk.
the design of health risk assessment instruments and how they can be improved to better meet the needs of both providers and patients.
the development and implementation of health risk assessment strategies that are designed to improve health outcomes and reduce healthcare costs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the implementation of health risk assessment with family health history information is a promising approach that can be beneficial to individuals, healthcare providers and the healthcare system as a whole.
family health history information can be successfully incorporated into a health risk assessment to improve patient care and to promote disease prevention.
the benefits of health risk assessments outweigh the barriers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
health risk assessments are a powerful tool for improving the overall health of the population.
health risk assessments can be a useful tool to promote health and prevent disease.
family history is an integral and valuable part of the risk assessment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

health risk assessments can be designed to be both useful and easy to use for patients and providers, and that they can provide a valuable service in helping individuals to better manage their health.
health risk assessments are a valuable and underutilised tool for improving health and health care.

health risk assessments can be an effective way to engage patients, families and communities in their own health and wellness, and that the use of family health history in these assessments is a powerful tool for improving health outcomes.
